proposed.text: Trap #29 identifies a counterintuitive emergency call button placement rule. At what height must the emergency call button in an accessible toilet be mounted, and why does it deviate from the standard operable controls range?

options.text: 900–1200 mm AFF — the same as all operable controls, to maintain design consistency
400–600 mm AFF — reachable from the floor by a fallen user who cannot stand or reach higher
300 mm AFF — at the base of the wall so it is always visible and reachable when crawling
700–800 mm AFF — consistent with the lower accessible handrail height and seated reach range

rationale.summary: Trap #29: emergency button at 400–600 mm AFF — reachable from the floor by a fallen user.
rationale.explanation: Trap #29 in the article. The standard operable controls range is 900–1200 mm AFF, but the emergency call button in an accessible toilet deliberately violates this range. The button must be at 400–600 mm AFF because it must be reachable by a user who has fallen to the floor and cannot stand or reach upward. A button at 900–1200 mm is unreachable by a prone or severely incapacitated user. This is one of the most counterintuitive specifications in BP 344 — the one control that is intentionally placed lower than the standard reach range.
common_misconceptions: Applying the standard 900–1200 mm operable range to the emergency button — this button is the explicit exception
Selecting 300 mm as 'even lower therefore better' — 400–600 mm is the specified range, not lower

proposed.explanation: Emergency toilet button: 400–600 mm AFF — the one control intentionally below the standard 900–1200 mm reach range.
